segments.text: In modest fashion, the colour by your face is the outfit. Online, you find out when it arrives.
Drape is one button any store adds to its product page.
No sign-up. Here we use the sample person; judges can try their own photo.
YouCam Facial Color Tones reads her skin, hair and eye colours from one face photo.
Drape turns that into an undertone and a contrast level: warm, high, gold. Colours that lift her, and colours that fight her.
The store's catalogue is re-sorted for her. Nothing is hidden. Every colour gets a plain verdict: yours, could work, or not your colour.
Then YouCam AI Clothes Virtual Try-On puts the same abaya on her own body, in two colours, side by side. Emerald lifts her face. Lavender washes it out. Look at the face, not the fabric.
YouCam Makeup Virtual Try-On adds the matching lip shade, and the palette picks her metal. Earrings try-on runs on live photos.
One tap sends the look to the cart.
It lands in the store's own bag. Drape never takes over the checkout.
Sometimes none of a garment's colours suit her. Normally, that is a lost sale, or a return.
YouCam AI Fabric re-makes her try-on in Sea Green Silk, a colour the store doesn't sell yet.
She asks the store to make it.
The seller sees that demand: colours tried, rejected and requested, plus every YouCam unit spent.
Opened on its own, Drape is a catalogue across partner stores, sorted by what suits you, with a Chrome extension for linked product pages.
Built for the Middle East and North Africa: full Arabic, right to left.
Drape. Buy the colour that suits you, not the one you send back.
